chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamza, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I perform Wudu and the water runs out, so I call the maid, but she is slow in bringing me the water, and my Wudu dries out.' He said, 'Repeat.'
ai.seo_question: What should one do if water runs out while performing Wudu?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling for *shakk* (doubt) in ablution when water is depleted before completion, ruling that the ablution must be repeated. This highlights the Shia principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) versus *ihtiyat* (precaution), emphasizing that uncertainty in the validity of a prior act of worship requires renewal to ensure ritual purity. The context underscores the practical application of juristic principles when resources are limited during the performance of obligatory acts.
